title: Class guides: levelling each class on WoW Forever
about: Per class: the levelling spec and talent path, stat priority, key trainer spells, how to solo, the dungeon role, class quests, common mistakes, the respec moment and habits; each statement with its class, topic and levels, sourced (official, datamined, guide authors) and summarised in our own words. `paths` holds one talent pick per level from 10 to 60 per class, checked against Forever's current trees (tests/test_classguide.py). Read by wowstats.classguide (the MCP's class_guide and the character page).

statements.title: Arms two-hander by default
statements.text: Level as Arms with the slowest, hardest-hitting two-hander you can get. Most Forever guides start here because it is simple and kills fast.

statements.title: Protection for solo grinding
statements.text: Method recommends Protection with a one-hander and shield for solo questing and grinding, and Arms for duo or group play. Protection also handles AoE packs with little health loss.

statements.title: Fury once Death Wish is up
statements.text: Fury dual-wield works but is weak before 30 and needs more downtime. If you go Fury, aim for Death Wish around 30 and Bloodthirst at 40.

statements.title: 10-19: Improved Rend first
statements.text: Take Improved Rend first: Rend now scales with attack power, so the bleed matters. Then Deflection, Improved Overpower and Improved Charge.

statements.title: 20-29: Deep Wounds and 2H spec
statements.text: Get Deep Wounds at 20, finish Deflection, then Two-Handed Weapon Specialization (now 2/4/6%), Impale and the one-point Spearing Strike.

statements.title: 30-39: Sweeping Strikes, Weaponmaster
statements.text: Sweeping Strikes at 30, then Bloodthrill (2 points: Rend targets can enable Overpower), all five Weaponmaster and the first Improved Slam.

statements.title: 40-60: Mortal Strike, then Fury
statements.text: Mortal Strike at 40 and the second Improved Slam, then move to Fury: Cruelty, Unbridled Wrath, Lingering Rage, Enrage, Piercing Howl and Reckless Swings.

statements.title: What Forever changed in the trees
statements.text: Tactical Mastery (10 rage kept) is baseline at 14 and Improved Tactical Mastery is only 3 points. The old weapon specialisations are merged into Weaponmaster: axes and polearms get crit, maces and staves ignore armour, swords get extra attacks.

statements.title: Weapon first, then Strength
statements.text: Weapon damage beats everything, then Strength and attack power, then Stamina and Agility. Hit and crit are one shared stat each for melee, ranged and spells in Forever.

statements.title: Learn schedule
statements.text: Charge and Rend at 4, Thunder Clap 6, Hamstring 8, Bloodrage 10, Overpower 12, Revenge and Tactical Mastery 14, Victory Rush, Slam, Cleave and Retaliation 20, Execute 24, Berserker Rage 30, Whirlwind 36, Pummel 38. Train every rank of Heroic Strike and Rend.

statements.title: Victory Rush and the reworked basics
statements.text: Victory Rush is new at 20: usable for 20 seconds after a kill, heals 10% of max health, 30-second cooldown. Rend and Thunder Clap gained a lot of attack power scaling, and Retaliation, Recklessness and Shield Wall no longer share a cooldown.

statements.title: Slam is a real filler now
statements.text: Slam has a 1.5-second cast and a 15-second cooldown. Improved Slam cuts the cooldown by 2.5 or 5 seconds and the cast time, and Slam no longer resets your swing.

statements.title: Rage: Charge, then Bloodrage
statements.text: Rage drains out of combat, so fights start empty. Charge first, then Bloodrage (it puts you in combat). Rage from hits taken is about 20-40% of the damage, and crits give extra rage.

statements.title: Single and multi-mob pull
statements.text: Battle Shout, Charge, Rend on mobs that will live, Overpower whenever it lights up, Heroic Strike with spare rage. On two or more: Sweeping Strikes, Thunder Clap, Demoralizing Shout, Cleave.

statements.title: Spend cooldowns on bad pulls
statements.text: Warriors have little self-healing and crowd control. Avoid extra pulls; when one happens, use Retaliation, Intimidating Shout or a shield and Defensive Stance rather than dying with them unused.

statements.title: Dungeon weapons carry you
statements.text: Weapons are almost all of a warrior's damage, so plan dungeon runs for weapon upgrades: Smite's Mighty Hammer (Deadmines, 18), Heavehammer (Wetlands excavation, 24), Corpsemaker (RFK, 29).

statements.title: Tanking in Forever
statements.text: Protection tanks with a shield: Defensive Stance threat is +80% and Defiance adds 7/13/20% but only with a shield. Thunder Clap threat was lowered, so lean on Sunder Armor and Revenge.

statements.title: What to bring
statements.text: No reagents. Bring food for the Well Fed buff, health potions and elixirs for hard pulls. As DPS keep Battle Shout up (raid-wide since Oct 16) and Sunder for the group.

statements.title: Level 10 stance quest
statements.text: A race-specific class quest at 10 teaches Defensive Stance, Sunder Armor and Taunt. Do it straight away.

statements.title: Level 20 armour quest
statements.text: At 20 there is a chest-armour quest (Brutal Hauberk, or Fire Hardened Hauberk for some races). Quest givers come from Classic data and are not confirmed in Forever.

statements.title: The Affray and the Whirlwind weapon
statements.text: At 30 your trainer sends you to Fray Island for The Affray: Berserker Stance and Intercept. The follow-up chain ends with a Whirlwind Axe, Sword or Warhammer; it is hard at 30, so buy the parts or bring help.

statements.title: Common mistakes
statements.text: Bloodrage before Charge, keeping an old weapon, Defensive Stance with a two-hander while solo, dumping all rage into an overkill Execute, and swapping stance without planning for the rage loss.

statements.title: No forced respec
statements.text: Arms carries you to 60 with no respec. Dual Talent Specialization at 40 lets you keep Arms for questing and Protection for tanking; at 60 move to an end-game build.

statements.title: Retribution with a two-hander
statements.text: Level as Retribution: a slow two-hander, Seal of Command from 20 and Judgement plus Holy Strike on cooldown. Method, Warcraft Tavern and ForeverDB's 'Seal of Command leveling' build all point here.

statements.title: When Protection or Holy instead
statements.text: Protection (Seal of Fury plus Consecration) suits pulling three or four mobs at once and tanking dungeons on the way. A Holy 'Shockadin' build hits harder than expected but is slower; pick it for duo play or if you want to heal groups.

statements.title: 10-19: mana first
statements.text: Benediction 5/5 first (cheaper Judgement, Holy Strike and seals), then Improved Judgement 2/2 and Conviction 3/3. Conviction now gives 2/4/6% crit to every spell and attack.

statements.title: 20-29: Seal of Command core
statements.text: Seal of Command at 20, Pursuit of Justice 2/2 (15% run speed), Sanctified Judgement 3/3, Two-Handed Weapon Specialization 3/3, Sacred Arbiter, and the first point of Vengeance at 30.

statements.title: 30-40: Vengeance to Unsealed Wrath
statements.text: Finish Vengeance 3/3, put one point in Unsealed Wrath's helpers (Unyielding Faith to reach 25 points, Repentance for the arrow), Champion of the Light 5/5, then Unsealed Wrath at 40. ForeverDB's level-40 checkpoint is exactly this set.

statements.title: 41-60: Holy for damage
statements.text: Spend the last 20 points in Holy: Divine Strength 5/5 and Improved Seals 5/5 first, then Healing Light, Reverence, Purifying Power, Divine Favor and Holy Conduit (ForeverDB). Method and Kami-labs swap the tail for Protection's Precision or Divine Intellect.

statements.title: What Forever changed in the trees
statements.text: Vengeance stacks to 5 and needs Seal of Command; Two-Handed Weapon Specialization gives 2/4/6% Physical and Holy damage; Champion of the Light adds 12-60% of Intellect as spell damage; Unsealed Wrath is the new 31-point talent. Twist of Light, Instrument of Law, One-Handed Weapon Specialization and Improved Seal of Fury are gone, and Divine Intellect moved to Protection.

statements.title: Stat priority (Retribution)
statements.text: Strength first, then Stamina, then spell power and Intellect (Champion of the Light turns Intellect into spell damage), armour last. Method adds that weapon upgrades come first in Forever because ability damage was lowered.

statements.title: Two-handers to chase
statements.text: Slow two-handers feed Holy Strike and Seal of Command: Forsaken Greataxe (15, Horde), Ironforge Greathammer (16, Alliance), Crested Scepter (24, Blackfathom Deeps), Debt Collector (26, Stockade), Heavehammer (31), Bonebiter (34, Alliance). Polearms can be trained from 20.

statements.title: Trainer spells that matter
statements.text: Seal of Righteousness and Holy Light at 1-2, Judgement and Blessing of Might at 4, Holy Strike at 6, Hammer of Justice at 8, Righteous Fury and Seal of Fury at 10, Blessing of Wisdom at 14, Retribution Aura at 16, Consecration, Exorcism, Flash of Light and Blessing of Kings at 20, Divine Shield at 32, Hammer of Wrath at 44.

statements.title: Forever's Judgement and Holy Strike
statements.text: Judgement no longer consumes your seal, its debuffs last 40 seconds and it is off the global cooldown, so press it whenever it is ready. Holy Strike (6) is a new baseline instant that adds Holy damage to a weapon hit.

statements.title: Consecration and blessings
statements.text: Consecration and Blessing of Kings are baseline at 20; Consecration only does full damage to 4 targets. Blessings and Greater Blessings last an hour, and Lay on Hands is on a 20-minute cooldown, so use it.

statements.title: Early pull pattern
statements.text: Seal of Righteousness up, Judgement as you close in, then Holy Strike; keep both on cooldown and auto-attack between. Heal with Holy Light only after a fight, not to full mid-fight.

statements.title: Seal of Command loop
statements.text: From 20 with a slow two-hander: Seal of Command, Judgement, Holy Strike, white hits, Hammer of Wrath from 44 to finish. Save Consecration for three or more mobs; it drains mana fast in the open world.

statements.title: Undead paladin mana
statements.text: Undead paladins can Cannibalize a humanoid or undead corpse for 7% health and mana every 2 seconds, which covers most rests after Holy Strike-heavy fights.

statements.title: Tanking as Protection
statements.text: Righteous Fury (10) adds 33% threat and 90% extra threat from Holy damage; Seal of Fury's Judgement taunts for 3 seconds. Protection with a shield and Consecration can tank dungeons as soon as Righteous Fury is trained at 10.

statements.title: What a Retribution paladin brings
statements.text: Buffs: Blessing of Might, Wisdom or Kings (an hour each), an aura, and Lay on Hands. Salvation is gone from Forever, so tanks lean on their own threat bonuses.

statements.title: Redemption quest at 12
statements.text: Alliance paladins get Redemption from The Tome of Divinity. Undead paladins do the new seven-part A Lesson in Divinity, starting with Danitha Morr at Bandarion Keep in Tirisfal Glades.

statements.title: Level-20 weapon quests
statements.text: Alliance: Verigan's Fist from The Test of Righteousness. Horde: Wolfsbane, whose chain includes the elite Old Fire Eye. Warcraft Tavern also lists Cloak of the Divine Storm at 22.

statements.title: Mount quests
statements.text: Paladins get a class warhorse at 40 and start a long epic charger chain at 60; Undead paladins have their own version.

statements.title: Re-sealing after Judgement
statements.text: Judgement keeps your seal in Forever, so recasting the seal after each Judgement wastes mana and a global cooldown.

statements.title: Consecration on big pulls
statements.text: Consecration hits only 4 targets at full damage; dropping it on big packs or single mobs burns the mana you need for Holy Strike.

statements.title: Following beta builds
statements.text: Builds naming Twist of Light, Instrument of Law, Improved Seal of Fury, One-Handed Weapon Specialization, Improved Holy Strike or a five-rank Conviction are from the beta and cannot be taken now.

statements.title: Dual spec at 40
statements.text: Dual specialization unlocks at 40 (Method: 50 gold at any paladin trainer). Keep Retribution for questing and set the second spec to Protection or Holy for dungeons.

statements.title: Optional Holy detour
statements.text: Method's alternative: after Pursuit of Justice, put points into Holy (Divine Strength, Improved Seals, Holy Conduit) and stay on Seal of Righteousness to about 32, then go back to Retribution. Talents are reset at a class trainer in a major city.

statements.title: Judge, then strike
statements.text: Judgement keeps the seal and is off the global cooldown, so it costs nothing to press on the way in.
statements.action: Judge as you close in, then Holy Strike; never recast the seal after judging

statements.title: Seal of Command at 20
statements.text: Seal of Command and Holy Strike scale with slow weapon speed.
statements.action: Equip the slowest two-hander you have and keep Seal of Command up

statements.title: Consecration only on packs
statements.text: It is full damage on 4 targets and expensive.
statements.action: Cast Consecration only when 3 or more mobs are on you

statements.title: Hammer of Wrath finish
statements.text: Hammer of Wrath is usable below 20% health.
statements.action: Finish mobs under 20% health with Hammer of Wrath

statements.title: Beast Mastery to level
statements.text: Beast Mastery is the levelling spec in every Forever guide: the pet tanks and does much of the damage, and Summon Hawk adds more from 25.

statements.title: Marksmanship and Survival
statements.text: Marksmanship does more damage itself and drinks less, but the pet holds less threat; skip Lone Wolf while levelling. Survival is a melee hybrid that only becomes a real melee spec at 30 and is harder to level.

statements.title: 10-19: Deadly Aspects first
statements.text: Five points in Deadly Aspects, two in Focused Fire, two in Improved Revive Pet, then one Endurance Training to open the next row.

statements.title: 20-29: Pathfinding and Summon Hawk
statements.text: Pathfinding at 20, Bestial Swiftness, Unleashed Fury, Summon Hawk at 25, then the first points of Ferocity.

statements.title: 30-40: Intimidation to Bestial Wrath
statements.text: Intimidation at 30, Bestial Discipline (less drinking), finish Ferocity, four points of Frenzy, then Bestial Wrath at 40.

statements.title: 41-60: twenty points in Marksmanship
statements.text: With 31 points in Beast Mastery, the last 20 go to Marksmanship: Lethal Attacks, Careful Aim, Rapid Killing, Efficiency, Trueshot Aura at 56 and four Mortal Shots.

statements.title: What Forever changed in the trees
statements.text: Deadly Aspects replaced Improved Aspect of the Hawk, Thick Hide merged into Endurance Training, and Intimidation now needs Bestial Swiftness. Summon Hawk (16-point talent) sends a hawk for 18 seconds, up to two at once, sharing a cooldown with Arcane Shot.

statements.title: Agility, then attack power
statements.text: Agility first, then ranged attack power, crit and hit; Intellect matters because mana limits you. Your ranged weapon gives most of your own damage, the rest is stat sticks. Survival also wants Strength and melee attack power.

statements.title: Learn schedule
statements.text: Serpent Sting 4, Arcane Shot and Hunter's Mark 6, Concussive Shot 8, Aspect of the Hawk and your pet 10, Mend Pet 12, Multi-Shot 18, Aimed Shot, Freezing Trap and Aspect of the Cheetah 20, Rapid Fire 26, Frost Trap 28, Feign Death 30.

statements.title: Shot buffs in Forever
statements.text: Aimed Shot is baseline at 20 with about 110% more bonus damage, and it shares a cooldown with Multi-Shot, not Arcane Shot. Arcane Shot (+30%) and Serpent Sting (+20%) were buffed and Aspect of the Hawk gives 20 to 110 ranged attack power by rank.

statements.title: Auto Shot and traps
statements.text: Auto Shot now needs you to stand still for 0.5 seconds. Traps work in combat, all share a 30-second cooldown, and you can have one fire and one frost trap out at once.

statements.title: Other baseline changes
statements.text: Scorpid Sting now lowers the target's hit chance by 2%, Disengage drops twice the threat, and Aspect of the Beast also gives melee attack power. Hunter's Mark ranks no longer stack.

statements.title: Pet tanks, you shoot
statements.text: Send the pet first and let it build threat, then Hunter's Mark, Serpent Sting on mobs that will live, Aimed Shot. Mend Pet at about half pet health; Concussive Shot or Wing Clip if a mob turns on you.

statements.title: Keep two hawks up
statements.text: From 25 keep two hawks and the pet attacking. Recast Summon Hawk late, just as one expires; after that Arcane Shot is mostly a filler on long fights or nearly dead targets.

statements.title: Mana, ammo and the dead zone
statements.text: Keep enough mana for Feign Death, stock ammo before leaving town, and step out of the 8-yard dead zone. Aspect of the Cheetah dazes you when hit, so drop it before the fight.

statements.title: Pets: cat or boar
statements.text: A cat is the top damage levelling pet; a boar is sturdier and its Charge grabs threat fast. Pet damage is normalised by family attack speed in PvE, and pets keep their innate attack-speed passive.

statements.title: Pets scale with your gear
statements.text: Pets get stats from your gear and no longer take player stat buffs. Tame Beast does not work on beasts above your level. Every family has one unique ability (Bear Swipe, Boar Charge, Cat Prowl, Raptor Savage Rend...).

statements.title: Ranged DPS in groups
statements.text: Turn Growl off so the pet doesn't steal the tank's mobs, use Freezing Trap on an add, and let the tank pull. Trueshot Aura is raid-wide once you have it.

statements.title: What to bring
statements.text: Full quiver or ammo pouch, pet food, food and water, health and mana potions. First Aid is your only cure for poisons, diseases and bleeds.

statements.title: Taming the Beast at 10
statements.text: The level-10 Taming the Beast chain gives Tame Beast and your first pet (Skyborne do it on Zephras Isle). ForeverDB found no other hunter class quests from 11 to 30.

statements.title: Non-class ranged weapon quests
statements.text: No hunter weapon class quest, but Hemet Nesingwary's chain (Welcome To The Jungle) ends with Master Hunter's Rifle or Bow (28, best done near 41), and 25 library books buy Truthseeker's Bow at 40.

statements.title: Common mistakes
statements.text: Shooting before the pet has threat, Raptor Strike after 10, recasting hawks too early, standing in the dead zone, running out of ammo or pet food, fighting in Aspect of the Cheetah, and trusting Feign Death (it can miss).

statements.title: No respec needed
statements.text: Beast Mastery to 40 then Marksmanship to 60 needs no respec. Dual Talent Specialization arrives at 40 if you want a second build; at 60 switch to an end-game build.

statements.title: Combat to level
statements.text: Combat is the solo levelling spec: it works with any one-hander and you don't need to be behind the mob.

statements.title: Subtlety or Assassination instead
statements.text: Method suggests Subtlety for groups, or from about 30 if you loot a strong dagger. Assassination gets good once Venom (30) and Mutilate (40) arrive but is not a starter spec.

statements.title: 10-19: cheaper Sinister Strike
statements.text: Start Combat with Efficient Strikes (cheaper Sinister Strike) and Coup de Grace (bigger Eviscerate), then Deflection. Kami-Labs also puts 2 points in Remorseless Attacks.

statements.title: 20-29: Precision and Riposte
statements.text: Precision, Riposte, Endurance, one Lightning Reflexes, Weapon Expertise and the first point of Aggression.

statements.title: 30-39: Blade Flurry and Hack and Slash
statements.text: Finish Aggression, Blade Flurry at 32, then Hack and Slash, Dual Wield Specialization (2 points, 25/50% off-hand damage) and Flash of Steel for Shank.

statements.title: 40-60: Adrenaline Rush, then Assassination
statements.text: Finish Flash of Steel, Adrenaline Rush at 42, max Hack and Slash and take Flawless Execution. The last points go into Assassination: Malice, Improved Slice and Dice, Lethality, Vigor, Blood Splatter and Cold Blood.

statements.title: What Forever changed in the trees
statements.text: Hack and Slash replaced the weapon specialisations and works with any weapon. Improved Sinister Strike became Efficient Strikes and Improved Eviscerate became Coup de Grace. Murder, Quietus, Cutthroat, Thousand Cuts and Improved Distract are gone.

statements.title: Weapon, then Agility
statements.text: Weapon DPS gives the biggest jump, then Agility and attack power; Strength is weaker. Later on, crit and hit (Precision covers poisons too) become worth more.

statements.title: Weapons for Combat
statements.text: Combat wants a non-dagger with the highest DPS in the main hand, since Sinister Strike scales off it. Rogues can now train one-handed axes; daggers, axes and thrown are known by default.

statements.title: Learn schedule
statements.text: Slice and Dice, Sap and Sprint at 10, Kick 12, Garrote and Expose Armor 14, Feint 16, Ambush and Poised 18, Rupture 20, Vanish 22, Shank 24, Cheap Shot 26, Kidney Shot 30, Blind 34.

statements.title: Shank and Poised are new
statements.text: Shank (24, rank 2 at 44) costs 5 energy, can't miss, hits with the off-hand for 50% weapon damage and gives back 15 energy (25 at rank 2), on a 10-second cooldown. Poised (18): at full energy out of combat your next ability costs 10 less.

statements.title: Poisons are much stronger
statements.text: Poisons start at 20; ForeverDB's client data has Instant at 20 and Deadly at 30. Their attack power scaling doubled, they have more charges, and they now stack with sharpening stones and Windfury. Run Instant and Deadly once you have both.

statements.title: Sap, Expose Armor and Feint changes
statements.text: Sap no longer breaks Stealth. Expose Armor now equals five Sunders and no longer blocks Sunder Armor. Feint drops twice as much threat.

statements.title: Basic loop
statements.text: Walk up and attack normal mobs; Stealth openers slow you down. Build with Sinister Strike, press Shank on cooldown, keep Slice and Dice up, then Eviscerate.

statements.title: Combo points and control
statements.text: Combo points stay on the target, so spend them before you switch. On two mobs: Sap or Gouge one, Evasion early, Blade Flurry from 32. Carry food and bandages: rogues have no heals.

statements.title: Melee DPS in groups
statements.text: Let the tank pull, use Feint to shed threat, and Backstab or Sinister Strike from behind. Keep Slice and Dice up and use Expose Armor only on long fights with other physical damage dealers.

statements.title: What to bring
statements.text: Poisons on both weapons, Flash Powder for Vanish, Blinding Powder for Blind, Thistle Tea for burst energy, health potions and food. Lockpicking opens some dungeon shortcuts.

statements.title: Poisons class quest at 20
statements.text: Poisons come from a class quest at 20 (Classic names like Mathias and the Defias or Deep Cover). ForeverDB says the Forever route is not confirmed, so treat the quest names as unverified.

statements.title: Blade of Cunning at 10
statements.text: Method lists Blade of Cunning, the reward of a level-10 class quest, as a strong early weapon.

statements.title: Ruby-Adorned Blade chain
statements.text: Method lists the Ruby-Adorned Blade as a class quest reward from level 30 on. Plan for it around 30.

statements.title: Common mistakes
statements.text: Opening every mob from Stealth, switching targets with unspent combo points, finishing with 1 or 2 points on healthy mobs, Backstab from the front or without a dagger, waiting too long on Evasion, keeping an old weapon.

statements.title: Respec only for a dagger
statements.text: Combat goes to 60 without a respec. Method's one respec moment: around 30, if you get a strong dagger and can afford it, switch to Subtlety. Dual Talent Specialization comes at 40.

statements.title: Shadow from 10, no respec
statements.text: Kami-labs (order taken from Mobalytics) levels as Shadow from the first point: Spirit Tap early, Mind Flay at 22, Vampiric Embrace at 27 and Shadowform at 42, then Discipline filler. Polestar's Shadow plan is the same idea with Shadowform at 40.

statements.title: Discipline wand route
statements.text: Discipline is the low-risk alternative: shield, Shadow Word: Pain and wand, with Penance from 30 and Power Infusion at 40 (Warcraft Tavern). Kami-labs' Discipline order (from Icy Veins) gets Penance later, at 38.

statements.title: Holy is for dungeon healers
statements.text: Holy kills too slowly to be a solo levelling spec. Pick it only if you plan to spend most of the climb healing dungeons.

statements.title: Shadow levelling: key talents by level
statements.text: Ends near 13/0/38. Key talents and the level to have them by: Improved Shadow Word: Pain 2 by 15; Spirit Tap 5 by 16; Mind Flay by 23; Vampiric Embrace by 27; Shadowform by 41; Silence by 45.

statements.title: What Forever changed in the trees
statements.text: Wand Specialization is 2 points, Shadow Focus gives Shadow hit, Vampiric Embrace is a 16-point talent, Shadowform the 31-point capstone, Penance a 21-point Discipline talent. Spirit Tap still exists (Shadow row 1, 5 ranks) in the current client data.

statements.title: Polestar's straight Shadow line
statements.text: Polestar spends all 31 points from 10 to 40 in Shadow (Spirit Tap 5, Improved Shadow Word: Pain 2, Improved Mind Blast, Mind Flay at 20, Vampiric Embrace at 28, Darkness 5) so Shadowform lands at 40, then fills Discipline from 41.

statements.title: Holy Binding replaced Binding Heal
statements.text: Binding Heal was removed on Nov 2. Its Holy slot is now Holy Binding: Flash Heal on someone else also heals you for half as much. Builds that still list Binding Heal are out of date.

statements.title: Stat priority
statements.text: Intellect and spell damage (Shadow damage for Shadow) first, then Stamina and Spirit, then armour. Until about 40 the wand is your biggest damage upgrade, so treat wand DPS as a top stat.

statements.title: Key trainer levels
statements.text: Shadow Word: Pain 4, Power Word: Shield 6, Mind Blast 10, Inner Fire 12, Psychic Scream 14, Devouring Plague and Fear Ward 20, Divine Spirit 30, Shadow Word: Death 32, Mind Flay rank 3 at 40, Prayer of Fortitude 48.

spells.name: Shadow Word: Pain
spells.why: main damage over time and a free tag

spells.name: Power Word: Shield
spells.why: stops pushback on casts and wand

spells.name: Devouring Plague
spells.why: baseline for every race now; damage plus heal

statements.title: New baseline spells
statements.text: Fear Ward and Devouring Plague come at 20 for every race, Divine Spirit is baseline at 30 and Shadow Word: Death at 32. Fade's threat drop is doubled.

statements.title: Shadow Word: Death backfires
statements.text: If the target survives Shadow Word: Death you lose 30% of your maximum health (a miss costs nothing). Cast it only when it will kill.

statements.title: Skip ranks to afford the mount
statements.text: Method advises against buying every rank on a fresh server so the level-40 mount stays affordable; keep Inner Fire and Power Word: Fortitude current if you solo. Full training costs about 206 gold for every class.

statements.title: Pre-40 pull
statements.text: Shield, Mind Blast while it closes, Shadow Word: Pain, then wand it down; melee only when dry and wandless. Refresh shield and pain on tougher mobs.

statements.title: Shadowform pull
statements.text: Shield, Mind Blast, Shadow Word: Pain, Mind Blast on cooldown, Shadow Word: Death to finish, Mind Flay as filler. Shadowform halves Shadow mana costs and cuts physical damage taken.

statements.title: Tag with Shadow Word: Pain
statements.text: Damage over time tags a mob instantly, so open with Shadow Word: Pain when other players are hunting the same mobs.

statements.title: Spirit Tap and the five-second rule
statements.text: A beta tester got most of his mana back from Spirit Tap after kills and from staying out of casting with a longer Shadow Word: Pain plus wand, rather than from Meditation. Beta numbers; treat as a hint.

statements.title: Shield now refreshes
statements.text: Power Word: Shield can be recast over a shield of equal or higher rank, so you can top it up before a pull lands.

statements.title: Shadow can heal the run
statements.text: A Shadow priest can heal every levelling dungeon without a respec, a bit less mana-efficiently than a healing spec. Bring level-appropriate water; Holy is the pick if you mostly run dungeons.

statements.title: Buffs you bring
statements.text: Power Word: Fortitude, Divine Spirit (30) and Fear Ward for everyone, and Fade with double threat drop when you pull aggro.

statements.title: Racial spells by class quest
statements.text: Class quests at 10 and 20 teach the racial spells. Human: Divine Grace (10), Feedback. Dwarf: Desperate Prayer, Chastise (20). Night Elf: Starshards (10), Elune's Grace (20). Gnome: Confounding Flash (10), Contingency Plan (20). Undead: Touch of Weakness, Dark Sacrifice (20). Troll: Hex of Weakness, Shadowguard.

statements.title: Wand quests
statements.text: Sizzle Stick (Wailing Caverns, 15), Gravestone Scepter (Blackfathom Villainy, BFD, 18+), Charred Wand (Dangerous!, Hillsbrad, 19), Dancing Flame (Final Passage, Arathi, 26), Wand of Mana Concentration (Arcanic Enigma, Dalaran, 27).

statements.title: Common mistakes
statements.text: Levelling as Holy, Shadow Word: Death as a filler, going Shadow before about 28 with no spell power, a stale wand, and Psychic Scream into extra packs.

statements.title: Classic builds do not port
statements.text: Classic opens with Wand Specialization 5/5; Forever caps it at 2. Builds naming Binding Heal or Shadow Affinity predate the current tree.

statements.title: Respec at 40 if you went Discipline
statements.text: Method levels 1-39 on a sturdy, mana-cheap Discipline-leaning build, then respecs to Shadow at 40 for Shadowform. Respecs happen at a class trainer in a major city; dual spec also opens at 40.

statements.title: Respec at 60
statements.text: The levelling Shadow build is not an endgame build: plan a respec at 60.

statements.title: Pre-40 opener
statements.text: Shield first, then Mind Blast, Shadow Word: Pain and the wand.
statements.action: Shield, Mind Blast, Shadow Word: Pain, then wand the rest

statements.title: Execute only
statements.text: Shadow Word: Death costs 30% health when the target lives.
statements.action: Cast Shadow Word: Death only when it will finish the target

statements.title: Keep the wand current
statements.text: The wand is the main damage until 40.
statements.action: Swap to the best wand you can get at every quest hub until 40

statements.title: Tag first
statements.text: Damage over time tags instantly.
statements.action: Open with Shadow Word: Pain when others hunt the same mobs

statements.title: Enhancement all the way
statements.text: Level as Enhancement: melee with a slow two-hander, Stormstrike at 25, Windfury from 30. Method, Warcraft Tavern, Kami-labs and ForeverDB all level this way, and no respec is needed.

statements.title: Elemental and Restoration
statements.text: Elemental works from range but runs out of mana and its procs are uneven. Restoration kills slowly alone; keep it as the second spec from 40 rather than levelling in it.

statements.title: 10-19: crit and Intellect to AP
statements.text: Thundering Strikes 5/5, Mental Dexterity 3/3 (now 150% of Intellect as attack power), then Ancestral Knowledge 2/5. Kami-labs and ForeverDB's level-20 checkpoint agree.

statements.title: 20-29: Stormstrike and instant Ghost Wolf
statements.text: Shamanistic Focus at 20, Elemental Weapons 3/3, one more Ancestral Knowledge, Stormstrike at 25, then Improved Ghost Wolf 2/2 straight away for an instant, indoor-usable Ghost Wolf, and the first Flurry points.

statements.title: 30-40: Flurry, Maelstrom, Rage of the Farseer
statements.text: Finish Flurry 5/5, Mental Quickness 2/2, Maelstrom Weapon 5/5 and Rage of the Farseer at 40 (ForeverDB's level-40 checkpoint; Method lists Rage of the Farseer at 40). Kami-labs goes into Restoration's Tidal Focus and Mindfulness here instead.

statements.title: Enhancement levelling: key talents by level
statements.text: Ends near 6/34/11. Key talents and the level to have them by: Mental Quickness 2 by 41; Spirit Weapons by 43; Rage of the Farseer by 46.

statements.title: What Forever changed
statements.text: Stormstrike deals 150% normalized weapon damage on a 6-second cooldown, Maelstrom Weapon procs twice as often, Flurry gives 6-30% attack speed, and Improved Ghost Wolf moved down to the row that opens at 15 points. Lava Burst is gone (Call of Thunder replaced it) and Elemental Mastery is now Lightning Mastery.

statements.title: Stat priority (Enhancement)
statements.text: Weapon damage and speed first (Stormstrike and Windfury scale with the weapon), then Strength and Intellect (Mental Dexterity turns Intellect into attack power), hit and crit, Stamina. Guides disagree on Agility; see contradictions.

statements.title: Two-handers to chase
statements.text: Ironforge Greathammer (16, Alliance quest), Smite's Mighty Hammer or Rockslicer (18, Deadmines), Corpsemaker (29, Razorfen Kraul), then the Rage of the Storm quest weapon. Two-handed maces are trained in Ironforge or Thunder Bluff, axes in Ironforge or Orgrimmar.

statements.title: Trainer spells that matter
statements.text: Rockbiter and Lightning Bolt at 1, Earth Shock 4, Earthbind 6, Lightning Shield 8, Flame Shock and Flametongue 10, Fire Nova and Purge 12, Ghost Wolf, Frost Shock and Lesser Healing Wave 20, Magma and Mana Spring 26, Windfury Weapon and Reincarnation 30, Chain Lightning and Windfury Totem 32.

spells.name: Flame Shock
spells.why: opener DoT, refresh only when it runs out

spells.name: Searing Totem
spells.why: Fire totem quest; free single-target damage

spells.name: Fire Nova
spells.why: AoE burst through your Fire totem; threat is yours now

spells.name: Ghost Wolf
spells.why: 40% run speed; instant with Improved Ghost Wolf

spells.name: Lesser Healing Wave
spells.why: fast self-heal when a pull goes wrong

spells.name: Windfury Weapon
spells.why: main weapon imbue from 30, adds an extra swing

statements.title: Totem tools in Forever
statements.text: Totemic Projection was renamed Totemic Call: it pulls your totems to you on a 30-second cooldown. Call of the Elements (20) and Call of the Ancestors (30) drop a saved set of totems with one button.

statements.title: Spell tuning
statements.text: Lightning Bolt's base damage was raised on every rank, Chain Lightning casts in 2.5 seconds, and shocks are back to Classic damage. Windfury Weapon and Windfury Totem add an extra white swing.

statements.title: Early pulls
statements.text: Rockbiter on the weapon, Lightning Shield up, pull with Lightning Bolt, Earth Shock as it lands, then melee. Stoneclaw or Earthbind buys time if a second mob joins.

statements.title: Flame Shock and Searing Totem
statements.text: One mob at a time: Flame Shock, drop Searing Totem, melee, Earth or Frost Shock when off cooldown, recast Flame Shock only after it expires. Rockbiter stays better than Flametongue until 30.

statements.title: Windfury and Stormstrike
statements.text: Keep Lightning Shield and Windfury Weapon up, pull with Lightning Bolt, Flame Shock, Stormstrike on cooldown, Earth Shock as filler. At 5 Maelstrom Weapon stacks cast a quick Lightning Bolt or a heal.

statements.title: Movement and cooldowns
statements.text: Instant Ghost Wolf covers most travel before the 40 mount. Rage of the Farseer (40) is a self haste cooldown for elites or emergencies. Astral Recall is a second hearth on a 15-minute cooldown.

statements.title: Tanking low dungeons
statements.text: With a one-hander and shield, Rockbiter and Earth Shock hold single targets, and Fire Nova's threat now lands on you, which helps on packs.

statements.title: What to bring
statements.text: Totems are the group value: Strength of Earth, Mana Spring (26), Windfury Totem (32). Carry water, bandages and potions; keep Restoration as the dual spec from 40 for healing runs.

statements.title: Totem quests
statements.text: Earth totem at 4 (3 for Skyborne on Zephras Isle), Fire at 10, Water at 20, Air at 30. Each totem item must stay in your bags. Dwarf shamans do Water and Air in Ironforge; Alliance trainers are only in Coldridge Valley, Kharanos, Ironforge and Aerie Peak.

statements.title: Rage of the Storm chain
statements.text: After the Air totem: a Razorfen Kraul boss item, 20 totems from Dustwallow, Desolace, Swamp of Sorrows and Badlands mobs, then a level-40 elite event in Thousand Needles. Enhancement picks Rage of the Storm, a 3.60-speed two-handed mace with +10% Stormstrike damage; the choice is permanent.

statements.title: Too many totems
statements.text: Dropping every totem on every pull wastes mana and global cooldowns, and totem twisting no longer works. Use only what the fight needs.

statements.title: Untrained weapon skills
statements.text: Swapping to a weapon type you have not trained and then pulling dangerous mobs: train two-handed maces or axes first.

statements.title: Stale beta builds
statements.text: Builds with Lava Burst, Elemental Mastery, Totemic Projection or Improved Ghost Wolf before 25 come from the beta and are not possible now.

statements.title: Dual spec at 40
statements.text: No respec is needed while levelling. At 40, dual specialization lets you keep Enhancement and add Restoration for groups.

statements.title: Flame Shock, totem, melee
statements.text: The Method/Warcraft Tavern single-target loop.
statements.action: Flame Shock, drop Searing Totem, melee; Earth Shock any caster

statements.title: Stormstrike before shocks
statements.text: Stormstrike raises the damage of your next Earth Shock or Lightning Bolt.
statements.action: Stormstrike on cooldown, then Earth Shock while its bonus is up

statements.title: Spend Maelstrom
statements.text: Maelstrom Weapon makes the next Lightning Bolt faster and cheaper.
statements.action: At 5 Maelstrom stacks cast Lightning Bolt or a heal, never let it sit

statements.title: One useful totem
statements.text: Totems cost mana and a global cooldown each.
statements.action: Drop only the totem this fight needs

statements.title: Frost is the levelling spec
statements.text: Method, Kami-labs (Mobalytics order) and Warcraft Tavern all level Frost: slows, freezes, Ice Block and Ice Barrier keep you alive and it handles small groups.

statements.title: Fire and Arcane
statements.text: Fire needs crit to work, so it is weak early but good in dungeons. Arcane is strong solo but streaky and hard on mana; overcasting Arcane Blast drains you fast.

statements.title: Frost levelling: key talents by level
statements.text: Ends near 12/0/39. Key talents and the level to have them by: Improved Frostbolt 5 by 16; Ice Lance by 20; Ice Block by 27; Cold Snap by 33; Ice Barrier by 40.

statements.title: Method's variant
statements.text: Method matches that order to the early 40s (Ice Block at 25, Shatter, Fingers of Frost, Winter's Chill, Cold Snap, Ice Barrier), then goes Arcane: Improved Channeling 5, Arcane Concentration, Missile Barrage, Arcane Subtlety, Arcane Blast at 57, Arcane Meditation. 1-2 Improved Blizzard points are optional for area farming.

statements.title: Forever's Frost toolkit
statements.text: Ice Lance is a 10-point Frost talent: instant, 300% damage on frozen targets, 8-second cooldown shared with Fire Blast. Fingers of Frost lets Chill effects make targets count as frozen. Cold Snap is a 21-point talent with a 10-minute cooldown. Ice Barrier also adds 15% Frost damage for a minute.

statements.title: Removed and renamed talents
statements.text: Piercing Ice, Arcane Focus and the Frost Blast spell are gone. Elemental Precision is now Precision (3 points, 2/4/6% hit with all spells) and Improved Fireball is now Accelerant.

statements.title: Stat priority
statements.text: Frost and Fire: spell damage, then Intellect, mp5, Stamina, Spirit, armour. Arcane: Intellect first, then spell damage, Spirit, mp5. Method calls spell power the strongest stat and weapon or wand the biggest single upgrade.

statements.title: Key trainer levels
statements.text: Frostbolt and Conjure Water 4, Conjure Food 6, Polymorph and Arcane Missiles 8, Frost Nova 10, Arcane Explosion 14, Flamestrike 16, Blizzard, Blink and Evocation 20, Counterspell 24, Cone of Cold 26, Ice Armor 30, Mage Armor 34, Frostfire Bolt and portals 40.

spells.name: Polymorph
spells.why: take an add out of the fight

spells.name: Cone of Cold
spells.why: area slow, boosted by Winter's Chill

spells.name: Frostfire Bolt
spells.why: new: big hit plus slow and damage over time

statements.title: Which Frostbolt rank
statements.text: With Permafrost use max rank for the longest slow; without it rank 1 is a cheap kiting tool. Arcane Concentration, Frostbite and Fingers of Frost proc less from ranks learned more than 12 levels ago.

statements.title: Frostfire Bolt
statements.text: Learned at 40: a 3-second cast that counts as Fire and Frost, hits like Fireball and leaves a slowing damage-over-time effect, using your better school against the lower resistance.

statements.title: Training cost
statements.text: Training every class spell from 1 to 60 costs about 206 gold.

statements.title: Frost pull
statements.text: Frostbolt as the main spell; Ice Lance on anything frozen by Frostbite, Fingers of Frost or Frost Nova; Nova when they reach you and back off; Cone of Cold to slow or reposition.

statements.title: Mana between pulls
statements.text: Conjure a stack of water and food before leaving town, drink between pulls, and always keep enough mana for Frost Nova plus Blink.

statements.title: No more mass kiting
statements.text: Cone of Cold lasts less and Improved Blizzard's slow is capped at 40%, explicitly to stop big kite pulls. Small groups still work.

statements.title: Winter's Chill feeds Cone of Cold
statements.text: Frostbolt and Ice Lance stack Winter's Chill, and each stack adds 20% to Cone of Cold, so Cone becomes a single-target nuke too.

statements.title: Dungeon role
statements.text: Damage and utility: Arcane Intellect, conjured food and water, Remove Lesser Curse, Polymorph, and portals from 40. Arcane Subtlety lowers threat. Fire and Arcane do better in dungeons than in the open world.

statements.title: Blizzard when melee range is unsafe
statements.text: Use Blizzard on packs once the tank holds them, and watch threat: area damage on a weak tank is how mages die.

statements.title: Class quest chains
statements.text: Level 10: Alliance Mirror Lake and the Alliance-only Mage-tastic Gizmonitor; Horde Ju-ju Heaps and The Balnir Farmstead. Level 15: Manaweave Robe (Alliance) or Spellfire Robe (Horde). Level 26: Astral Knot Garment (Alliance) or Nether-lace Garment (Horde). Rewards are staves, off-hands, robes and wands.

statements.title: Icefury Wand
statements.text: The mage chain starting with Journey To The Marsh gives the Icefury Wand: usable at 30, comfortable at 40.

statements.title: Comprehension
statements.text: Forever adds Comprehension, a minor tradeskill: Comprehend Scroll reads scrolls that creatures drop.

statements.title: Common mistakes
statements.text: Overcasting Arcane Blast, Frost without Frost Channeling (mana-hungry), skipping drinks, Polymorph on a target that is not isolated, and area damage before the tank has threat.

statements.title: Stale builds
statements.text: Builds with Piercing Ice, Arcane Focus or Improved Fireball predate the current tree, and Classic Frost builds do not carry over.

statements.title: Respec only at 60
statements.text: Frost needs no respec while levelling. Method mentions 2 Wand Specialization points at 12-13 for players with spare gold, removed later by a respec. Plan a respec to an endgame build at 60.

statements.title: Ice Lance on frozen only
statements.text: Ice Lance does 300% on frozen targets.
statements.action: Ice Lance only frozen targets: after Frost Nova, Frostbite or Fingers of Frost

statements.title: Escape mana
statements.text: Nova plus Blink is the escape.
statements.action: Keep enough mana for Frost Nova plus Blink before every pull

statements.title: Conjure before leaving
statements.text: Free water saves gold and time.
statements.action: Conjure a stack of water before you leave town; drink after each pull

statements.title: Affliction is the levelling spec
statements.text: Method, Warcraft Tavern, Kami-labs (Mobalytics order) and Polestar all level Affliction: instant Corruption, drains and Siphon Life, no respec needed.

statements.title: Demonology and Destruction
statements.text: Demonology comes online late; Warcraft Tavern respecs into it at 27 for Demonic Brand. Destruction is the burst spec for dungeons and costs more mana.

statements.title: Affliction levelling: key talents by level
statements.text: Ends near 45/6/0. Key talents and the level to have them by: Improved Corruption 5 by 18; Fel Concentration 3 by 25; Siphon Life by 36; Amplify Curse by 38; Wrack by 50.

statements.title: Where the Affliction levelling guides differ
statements.text: Some builds take Demonic Embrace 5, Demonic Aegis 2, Fel Vitality 2 in place of Unholy Power, Soul Harvest, Amplify Curse; others Improved Shadow Bolt 5, Bane 5, Curse of Exhaustion 1 in place of Unholy Power, Malevolence, Improved Life Tap; others Bane 5, Cataclysm 3 in place of Unholy Power, Grim Reach, Fel Vitality.

statements.title: What Forever changed
statements.text: Improved Corruption also adds up to 10% Corruption damage. Wrack is the 31-point capstone and its coefficient was doubled on Nov 2. Removed for good: Improved Drain Life, Dark Pact, Fel Intellect, Fel Stamina, Improved Firebolt, Devastation, Improved Immolate.

statements.title: Stat priority
statements.text: Spell power (Shadow for Affliction), wand DPS until about 30, then Spirit and Intellect, then Stamina. Spirit counts for more than in Classic because Life Tap scales with it.

statements.title: Key trainer levels
statements.text: Shadow Bolt, Immolate and Demon Skin 1, Corruption 4, Life Tap 6, Bane of Agony and Fear 8, Drain Soul, Create Healthstone and the Voidwalker 10, Health Funnel 12, Drain Life 14, Searing Pain and Create Soulstone 18, Demon Armor and Ritual of Summoning 20, Soul Fire 48.

spells.name: Corruption
spells.why: core damage over time; instant with the talent

spells.name: Life Tap
spells.why: health to mana; scales with Spirit

spells.name: Bane of Agony
spells.why: main damage over time, coexists with a curse

spells.name: Demon Armor
spells.why: armour and health regen; never let it drop

statements.title: Banes and curses
statements.text: Curse of Agony and Curse of Doom became Banes, so a target carries one Bane and one Curse from you. Curse of the Elements covers every magic school and Curse of Shadows is gone.

statements.title: Life Tap and stones
statements.text: Life Tap scales with Spirit. Firestone and Spellstone are now weapon imbues that stack with wizard oils; Spellstone boosts Shadow damage only since Nov 2.

statements.title: Talent spells
statements.text: Siphon Life, Wrack, Shadowburn, Conflagrate and Incinerate are talents, not trainer spells. Warcraft Tavern's build takes Siphon Life at 37 and Wrack at 47, later than the tree allows.

statements.title: Pull and rest
statements.text: Send the demon first, Bane of Agony to pull, then Corruption and Immolate on mobs that will live; Drain Life from 30, wand the last bit. Life Tap when health is above mana, Drain Life when mana is above health; carry food.

statements.title: Pets
statements.text: Imp at 1, Voidwalker at 10 (the tank), Succubus or Incubus at 20, Felhunter at 30. Pets now get only 2 health per point of your Stamina, so the Voidwalker tanks worse than beta guides suggest. Buy every Torment rank.

statements.title: Drain-tanking from 30
statements.text: Let mobs hit you while damage over time and the pet work, and Drain Life back the health. Both guides say Drain Life is too weak for this before 30.

statements.title: Soul shards
statements.text: Drain Soul's shard chance on damage ticks was cut hard, so finish mobs with rank 1 Drain Soul and keep 2-3 spare. A Shadowburn kill refunds its shard.

statements.title: Dungeon role
statements.text: Damage dealer; Destruction is the burst spec for groups. Bring the Imp for Blood Pact, hand out Healthstones and summon latecomers with Ritual of Summoning.

statements.title: Curse of the Elements helps casters
statements.text: Curse of the Elements now covers every magic school, so it helps every caster in the group.

statements.title: Pet quests
statements.text: Voidwalker at 10: Gakin's Summons (Human), The Slaughtered Lamb (Gnome), Gan'rul's Summons (Orc, Troll), Halgar's Summons (Undead). Succubus at 20: Devourer of Souls; Incubus at 20: What Is Love? (Stormwind), Love Hurts (Orgrimmar), Hearts of the Lovers (Undercity). Felhunter at 30: Seeking Strahad.

statements.title: Item and mount quests
statements.text: Level 20: Staff or Orb of Soran'ruk (fragments from Blackfathom Deeps and Shadowfang Keep). Felsteed at 40, Dreadsteed chain at 60. Method also lists Soul Harvester at 50 (Trolls of a Feather).

statements.title: Common mistakes
statements.text: Searing Pain before Demonic Brand, Shadow Bolt on a feared mob, Curse of Recklessness on a mob you will fear, wanding at full mana, Drain Life at full health, damage over time on dying mobs, letting Demon Skin or Armor drop.

statements.title: Classic builds
statements.text: Classic builds with Improved Drain Life, Dark Pact, Fel Stamina or Fel Intellect cannot be made: those talents are gone.

statements.title: Respec moments
statements.text: Affliction levels 10-60 with no respec. Warcraft Tavern's Demonology plan respecs at 27; Kami-labs respecs at 60 into an endgame build.

statements.title: Pet first
statements.text: The pet takes the hits.
statements.action: Send the pet in first, then Bane of Agony and Corruption; wand the low end

statements.title: Balance health and mana
statements.text: Life Tap and Drain Life trade health and mana.
statements.action: Life Tap when health beats mana; Drain Life when mana beats health

statements.title: Shards
statements.text: Damage ticks rarely give shards now.
statements.action: Finish mobs with rank 1 Drain Soul until you hold 2-3 shards

statements.title: Armour up
statements.text: Demon Skin and Demon Armor give health regen.
statements.action: Recast Demon Skin or Demon Armor the moment it drops

statements.title: Feral, cat first
statements.text: Level as Feral: Bear Form from 10, Cat Form from 20, Cat for questing and Bear for bad pulls. Method, Warcraft Tavern and ForeverDB all lead with it.

statements.title: Balance, Restoration, hybrid
statements.text: Balance can level 1-60 (Multi-DoT with roots, or a slower Eclipse Starfire build); Method suggests it only after 30. Restoration kills too slowly solo. A hybrid Feral build tanks dungeons in Bear and still quests in Cat.

statements.title: 10-19: Ferocity and Feral Swiftness
statements.text: Ferocity 5/5 first (cheaper Claw, Rake, Maul, Swipe), Feral Swiftness 2/2 (Method's favourite early pick: cat run speed and dodge), then Furor. ForeverDB's level-20 checkpoint ends Ferocity 5, Furor 3, Feral Swiftness 2.

statements.title: 20-29: Cat damage
statements.text: Savage Fury 2/2, Sharpened Claws 2/2, Furor to 5/5, Predatory Strikes 3/3 and a point of Blood Frenzy, all from ForeverDB's level-30 checkpoint. Kami-labs takes Feral Charge at 22 here.

statements.title: 30-40: Leader of the Pack to Shifting Power
statements.text: Leader of the Pack at 30, Natural Instinct 2/2, Blood Frenzy 2/2, Predatory Discipline, Rend and Tear 5/5, then Shifting Power at 40, which Method picks over Primal Bite for cats.

statements.title: 41-60: bear tools and Heart of the Wild
statements.text: Primal Bite, Lacerate, Thick Hide 3/3, Shredding Attacks 3/3, Feral Instinct, Feral Charge, Natural Reaction 5/5, then Heart of the Wild 5/5 in Restoration (ForeverDB). Method and Kami-labs instead spend some points on Balance's Genesis, Nature's Majesty and Nature's Reach.

statements.title: What Forever changed in Feral
statements.text: Berserk is gone. Lacerate and Predatory Discipline are 1-point Feral talents, Primal Bite (needs Leader of the Pack) and Shifting Power (needs Predatory Discipline) sit in the bottom row, Furor and Heart of the Wild swapped trees, and Rend and Tear gives 3-15%.

statements.title: Forms use your weapon
statements.text: Cat and Bear auto-attacks now use the equipped weapon's DPS, and weapon enchants, procs, most potions and racials work in form. Weapon upgrades matter for Feral, unlike Classic.

statements.title: New baseline spells
statements.text: Nature's Grasp at 10 (castable in form and indoors), Revive at 12, Omen of Clarity as a baseline passive at 20, Faerie Fire usable in Cat and Bear at no cost, and Ferocious Bite gets a new rank 1 at 24.

statements.title: Damage and threat tuning
statements.text: Shred deals 200% weapon damage, Claw 140%, Ravage 435%, and Rip, Rake, Ferocious Bite and Pounce gained about 25%. Bear and Dire Bear threat is 115% to make up for the loss of Salvation.

statements.title: Trainer and quest spells
statements.text: Wrath and Healing Touch 1, Moonfire and Rejuvenation 4, Entangling Roots 8, Bear Form 10 (quest), Faerie Fire 18, Cat Form, Claw, Prowl, Rip and Shred 20, Rake and Ferocious Bite 24, Dash 26, Travel Form 30, Ravage and Poised 32, Pounce 36, Dire Bear Form and Innervate 40, Barkskin 44.

spells.name: Faerie Fire
spells.why: free in form, pulls without leaving Cat

spells.name: Ferocious Bite
spells.why: new rank 1; finisher for short fights

statements.title: Stat priority (Feral)
statements.text: Weapon DPS, then Strength, Agility and attack power, then Stamina, Intellect and Spirit, armour last (Warcraft Tavern). Method stresses Intellect and Spirit more because Shifting Power and the heals between pulls cost mana.

statements.title: Weapons to chase
statements.text: Smite's Mighty Hammer (18, Deadmines), Defender of Dalaran (30, Alliance quest), Scavenged Magram Armament (35, Desolace quest), The Pacifier (36), Grimlok's Charge (42, Uldaman). Polearms can be trained from 20.

statements.title: Caster levels
statements.text: Wrath and Moonfire, melee when out of mana, Rejuvenation to heal; keep Mark of the Wild and Thorns up.

statements.title: Bear levels
statements.text: Two Wraths and a Moonfire as it runs in, then Bear Form: Enrage, Demoralizing Roar, Maul; Swipe when there are several.

statements.title: Cat loop
statements.text: Prowl, open with Shred from behind (Ravage from 32), Faerie Fire, Rake, Claw to 4-5 combo points, then Rip on long fights or Ferocious Bite at 70+ energy. Combo points no longer drop when you switch target.

statements.title: Shifting Power and mana
statements.text: Use Shifting Power below 50 energy, but keep enough mana to heal between pulls with Regrowth, Rejuvenation or Healing Touch. Teleport: Moonglade works as a second hearth.

statements.title: Bear tank or cat DPS
statements.text: Bear tanks with 115% threat: Faerie Fire, Lacerate to 5 stacks, Primal Bite on cooldown, Maul or Swipe. As Cat, Leader of the Pack (30) gives the party crit. Carry Rebirth reagents and offer Innervate from 40.

statements.title: Form quests
statements.text: Bear Form at 10 (Heeding the Call; High Order Skyborne do The Great Ursera Spirit), Teleport: Moonglade at 10, Cure Poison at 14 (Lessons Anew), Aquatic Form at 16 (A Lesson to Learn, with the Idol of Shifting Tides), Cat Form at 20 (The Great Cat Spirit; Skyborne get The Great Windborne Cat Spirit).

statements.title: Level-50 Sunken Temple quest
statements.text: A Better Ingredient (Sunken Temple) offers Grizzled Pelt for Feral, Moonshadow Stave for Balance or Forest's Embrace for Restoration. There is no druid weapon quest before that.

statements.title: Late form quests
statements.text: Bear at 10 and Cat at 20 are the two big power spikes; staying in caster form while the quest waits slows everything.

statements.title: Wasted bleeds
statements.text: Rake and Rip on mobs that die in seconds or on mechanical targets waste energy; Ferocious Bite them instead.

statements.title: Overusing Shifting Power
statements.text: Spending all your mana on energy leaves nothing for heals between pulls, so you drink anyway.

statements.title: Stale beta builds
statements.text: Builds with Berserk, Heart of the Wild in Feral, Gift of the Earthmother, Tiger's Fury or a baseline Lacerate predate the November changes.

statements.title: Balance or dual spec
statements.text: No respec is needed for Feral. Method's optional switch to Balance comes after 30; dual specialization at 40 lets you keep Feral and add Restoration or a bear build for groups.

statements.title: Open from stealth
statements.text: Shred and Ravage do the most from behind and Prowl gives you the angle.
statements.action: Prowl in, open with Shred (Ravage from 32), then Rake and Claw

statements.title: Energy from mana
statements.text: Shifting Power trades mana for 40 energy.
statements.action: Cast Shifting Power under 50 energy only if mana is left for a heal

statements.title: Skip bleeds on dying mobs
statements.text: Bleeds need time to pay off.
statements.action: Skip Rake and Rip on mobs that will die within a few seconds

statements.title: Form quests on the day
statements.text: Bear and Cat are quest-gated in Forever.
statements.action: Do the Bear quest at 10 and the Cat quest at 20 as soon as you ding

contradictions.title: Crit rage: 75% or 100%
contradictions.text: The Sept 30 deep dive says crits give 75% more rage; ForeverDB says 100%. The Oct 1 notes split it: auto-attack crits 75%, other crits 100%. Follow the dev notes, they are the latest official word.

contradictions.title: Solo spec: Protection or Arms
contradictions.text: Method says Protection for solo and Arms for groups; Warcraft Tavern, ForeverDB and the Mobalytics-based Kami-Labs build start with Arms. Follow Arms as the default (more sources); switch to Protection if you keep dying solo.

contradictions.title: Stale talents in older builds
contradictions.text: Polestar (ForeverDB beta 1.60.1.70450) puts 5 points into Improved Tactical Mastery and Flurry; both are 3 points on the current tree (Nov 3 notes). wow.gg's September Arms sample also lists Bloodthrill at 5 and Sweeping Strikes at 2. Follow the current tree.

contradictions.title: Removed Fury talents still in guides
contradictions.text: The Sept 30 deep dive announced Boundless Rage, Raging Blows and a Fury Precision, and Warcraft Tavern still suggests Raging Blows. The Oct 1 notes removed Boundless Rage and the current tree has none of the three (Furious Precision replaced Precision). Ignore them.

contradictions.title: Spearing Strike and Deflection
contradictions.text: Warcraft Tavern skips Spearing Strike and takes Deflection to reach Anger Management; the Mobalytics order (Kami-Labs) takes Spearing Strike and no Anger Management; Method takes Improved Tactical Mastery. Followed Kami-Labs for the path since it is the only full 10-60 bracket list; all are legal.

contradictions.title: Righteous Fury level
contradictions.text: Warcraft Tavern's spell table puts Righteous Fury at 16; Blizzard's development notes (3 Nov) and Method say 10.

contradictions.title: First talents
contradictions.text: Kami-labs (from Mobalytics' guide) opens with Deflection 5/5; Method and ForeverDB's checkpoint open with Benediction.

contradictions.title: Champion of the Light
contradictions.text: Polestar's beta Retribution build skips Champion of the Light, citing a Retribution Aura spell-power bug; Method, Kami-labs and ForeverDB take it 5/5.

contradictions.title: Improved Righteous Fury
contradictions.text: Warcraft Tavern's September changes article says Improved Righteous Fury was removed; the current tree and the November development notes have it (3/6/9% less damage taken).

contradictions.title: Improved Holy Strike
contradictions.text: Warcraft Tavern's September article lists a 2-point Improved Holy Strike (12s to 10s cooldown); the current tree has none. Protection's Shieldsworn now cuts Holy Strike's cooldown by 4 seconds.

contradictions.title: Stale Polestar builds
contradictions.text: Polestar (beta 70450) names Holy Conduit in Retribution, Twist of Light, Instrument of Law, a five-rank Conviction, Divine Intellect in Holy, Improved Seal of Fury and One-Handed Weapon Specialization. The development notes removed or moved all of them; Holy Conduit still exists, but in Holy.

contradictions.title: Champion of the Light values
contradictions.text: The knowledge base says Champion of the Light converts 10/20/30% of Intellect; the development notes give 12/24/36/48/60% over 5 ranks.

contradictions.title: Trap cooldowns
contradictions.text: The Sept 30 deep dive gave Frost and Fire traps separate cooldowns, and Method still says Freezing Trap shares only with Frost Trap. The Nov 3 notes put all traps on one 30-second cooldown. Follow Nov 3.

contradictions.title: Deadly Aspects trigger
contradictions.text: The Sept 30 deep dive says Deadly Aspects procs from melee with Aspect of the Beast; the datamined tooltip (build 70959) says Auto Shot procs it while Aspect of the Hawk is active. Follow the tooltip: keep Hawk up.

contradictions.title: Efficiency or Hawk Eye
contradictions.text: Method spends 3 Marksmanship points on Efficiency; the Mobalytics order on Kami-Labs takes Hawk Eye instead. Followed Method, since Warcraft Tavern also prioritises Efficiency for mana.

contradictions.title: Endurance Training early
contradictions.text: ForeverDB's level-20 build puts 5 points in Endurance Training; Method and Kami-Labs take only 1 and push damage instead. Followed the two that agree.

contradictions.title: wow.gg September sample
contradictions.text: wow.gg's BM sample (Sept 19) uses Eagle Eye and 'Focus Fire'; the current tree has Hawk Eye and Focused Fire. Its 44-point BM split is a reference build, not a levelling order. Ignore it for levelling.

contradictions.title: Rapid Killing and Rapid Recuperation order
contradictions.text: The Sept 30 deep dive says Rapid Recuperation is the prerequisite for Rapid Killing; the current tree puts Rapid Killing on row 3 and Rapid Recuperation on row 5 with the arrow from Rapid Killing. Follow the tree.

contradictions.title: Stale talent names in Warcraft Tavern
contradictions.text: Warcraft Tavern's rogue page still names Improved Sinister Strike, Improved Eviscerate and Thousand Cuts. The Nov 3 notes renamed the first two (Efficient Strikes, Coup de Grace) and removed Thousand Cuts. Follow the notes and the current tree.

contradictions.title: Polestar builds predate the Nov 2 rework
contradictions.text: Polestar (ForeverDB beta 1.60.1.70450) uses Murder, Quietus, Thousand Cuts, Improved Sinister Strike, Improved Eviscerate and 5-point Lethality and Dual Wield Specialization. None of that is on the current tree. Kami-Labs' Nov 12 Combat order matches the tree, so the path follows it.

contradictions.title: wow.gg September sample
contradictions.text: wow.gg's Combat sample (Sept 19) lists Improved Sinister Strike, Restless Blades, Surprise Attacks and 5-point Dual Wield Specialization. None exist now; ignore it.

contradictions.title: Venom and Mutilate redesign
contradictions.text: The Oct 7 deep dive made Venom a 25-energy finisher and Mutilate a 21-point talent needing two daggers. The Nov 3 notes made Venom a passive Shank buff (row 5) and moved Mutilate to the bottom row. Follow Nov 3.

contradictions.title: Crit or Agility first
contradictions.text: Warcraft Tavern puts crit chance first from 10; Method puts Agility and attack power first and says weapon DPS matters most. Follow Method: crit on levelling gear is rare and Agility already gives some.

contradictions.title: Does Spirit Tap exist?
contradictions.text: The knowledge base doubted Spirit Tap because Blizzard's deep dive never mentions it. The current client data (ForeverDB, build 70959) has Spirit Tap in Shadow row 1 with 5 ranks. Follow the client data: it exists.

contradictions.title: Binding Heal
contradictions.text: Blizzard's deep dive and Warcraft Tavern's table list Binding Heal as a Holy talent, and Polestar's Holy build takes it at 31. The Nov 2 dev notes removed it for Holy Binding, which is what the current tree has. Follow the dev notes and tree.

contradictions.title: Shadow Word: Death self-damage
contradictions.text: The Sept 30 deep dive says 10% of maximum health on a survivor; the Nov 2 dev notes raised it to 30% and made misses free. Follow the later dev notes.

contradictions.title: When Shadowform comes
contradictions.text: Method goes Discipline to 39 and respecs at 40; Kami-labs (Mobalytics order) stays Shadow from 10 but spends 2 points on Wand Specialization, so Shadowform waits until 42; Polestar goes pure Shadow and gets it at 40. The talent path follows Kami-labs: a cited guide, legal on the current tree, no respec gold. Pick Polestar's line if 2 levels of Shadowform matter more than the wand bonus.

contradictions.title: Penance timing in Discipline
contradictions.text: Warcraft Tavern takes Penance at 30, the earliest the tree allows; Kami-labs' Discipline order (from Icy Veins) takes it at 38. Take it at 30 if you level as Discipline: it is your best attack.

contradictions.title: Shadow Affinity
contradictions.text: Blizzard's deep dive describes a changed Shadow Affinity talent, but the current Shadow tree has no talent of that name. Treat it as removed.

contradictions.title: Agility for Enhancement
contradictions.text: Method ranks Agility > Strength > Stamina > Intellect; Warcraft Tavern ranks hit > Strength > Intellect > crit > spell damage > Agility.

contradictions.title: Totemic Projection vs Totemic Call
contradictions.text: Warcraft Tavern's spell table lists Totemic Projection at 22 (and Totemic Recall at 20); the development notes renamed Totemic Projection to Totemic Call with a 30-second cooldown.

contradictions.title: Lava Burst
contradictions.text: Warcraft Tavern's guide and Polestar's Elemental build still use Lava Burst at 30; the development notes removed it for Call of Thunder.

contradictions.title: Mid-level talents
contradictions.text: Kami-labs (from Mobalytics) spends 30-49 on Improved Stormstrike, Restoration (Tidal Focus, Mindfulness, Totemic Focus, Water Shield) and delays Maelstrom Weapon; ForeverDB has Mental Quickness, Maelstrom Weapon 5/5 and Rage of the Farseer by 40.

contradictions.title: Improved Ghost Wolf timing
contradictions.text: Polestar takes Improved Ghost Wolf at 18; on the current tree it needs 15 Enhancement points, so 25 at the earliest (Method: right after Stormstrike).

contradictions.title: Polestar names removed talents
contradictions.text: Polestar's Frost build takes Piercing Ice and Arcane Focus, and its Fire build Improved Fireball. The Nov 2 dev notes and the current tree removed the first two and renamed the third Accelerant. Ignore those picks.

contradictions.title: Deep dive vs launch tree
contradictions.text: The Oct 7 deep dive names Wake of Fire, a 5-rank Elemental Precision and Missile Barrage as a 16-point talent. The current tree has Improved Fire Blast, a 3-rank Precision and Missile Barrage on row 2. Follow the current tree.

contradictions.title: Last 15 points
contradictions.text: Kami-labs (Mobalytics) spends 40-49 in Frost (Frost Channeling, Improved Blizzard) then 12 Arcane points without Arcane Blast; Method goes Arcane from 43 with Arcane Blast at 57 and Arcane Meditation. The path follows Kami-labs because Warcraft Tavern also warns Frost runs dry without Frost Channeling.

contradictions.title: Arcane opener for Frost
contradictions.text: Warcraft Tavern's beta Frost build opens with 7 Arcane points for Missile Barrage; Method and Kami-labs open with Improved Frostbolt 5. Follow the Frost-first order: two guides agree and it reaches Ice Lance at 20.

contradictions.title: Cold Snap and Ice Barrier are talents
contradictions.text: Method's spell table lists Cold Snap at 34 and Ice Barrier at 40 like trainer spells. Both are Frost talents (Cold Snap needs 20 points, Ice Barrier 30 and Cold Snap); the Kami-labs order gets them at 32 and 40.

contradictions.title: Four Affliction orders
contradictions.text: Warcraft Tavern (41/7/3, pet talents at 18-24), Kami-labs from Mobalytics (40/0/11, Destruction last), Method (Suppression first, Demonology at 46) and Polestar (31/20/0) differ after the shared Improved Corruption opener. The path follows Warcraft Tavern: the only one with a full level-by-level order that is legal on the current tree.

contradictions.title: Siphon Life and Wrack timing
contradictions.text: Warcraft Tavern's ability table puts Siphon Life at 30 and Wrack at 40 (the earliest the tree allows), but its build takes them at 37 and 47. Follow the build order in the path; taking them earlier is legal if you skip earlier points.

contradictions.title: Grim Reach and Malediction
contradictions.text: Blizzard's deep dive lists Grim Reach as removed and Malediction as added; the current tree has Grim Reach and no Malediction. Follow the tree.

contradictions.title: Shadowburn and Conflagrate levels
contradictions.text: Method lists Shadowburn at 24 and Conflagrate at 29; Warcraft Tavern takes them at 20 and 25. Both are Destruction talents, reachable at 20 and 25 with points in that tree; the trainer only sells later ranks.

contradictions.title: Drain Soul shards
contradictions.text: The deep dive promised a growing per-tick shard chance that ends guaranteed; the Nov 2 dev notes cut the tick chance sharply. Follow the dev notes: finish with Drain Soul.

contradictions.title: Feral gear stats
contradictions.text: Warcraft Tavern puts Strength, Agility and attack power first for Feral; Method says Feral levelling gear should favour Intellect and Spirit.

contradictions.title: Tiger's Fury
contradictions.text: Kami-labs (26 Sep, beta) lists Tiger's Fury at 24 with +15% damage; Warcraft Tavern (30 Sep) says it was removed for Shifting Power, and its current spell table has none at 24.

contradictions.title: Lacerate baseline or talent
contradictions.text: Warcraft Tavern's September deep dive lists Lacerate as a baseline spell at 42; the November development notes make it a 1-point Feral talent (25 at the earliest).

contradictions.title: Capstone at 40
contradictions.text: Method picks Shifting Power over Primal Bite; ForeverDB's cat-and-bear checkpoint takes Primal Bite at 40 and Shifting Power by 50.

contradictions.title: Kami-labs order
contradictions.text: Kami-labs (from Mobalytics) opens with Furor 4 and Ferocity 4, puts Genesis and Nature's Majesty in the 30s and skips Shifting Power and Rend and Tear; ForeverDB and Method keep Feral points in Feral through 40.

contradictions.title: Stale Polestar Feral build
contradictions.text: Polestar (beta 70450) puts Heart of the Wild in Feral and takes Berserk and Gift of the Earthmother; the current tree has Heart of the Wild in Restoration and neither of the others.

contradictions.title: What Furor does
contradictions.text: The knowledge base says Furor keeps energy when you shift from Cat to Bear; Warcraft Tavern's September deep dive says energy is lost when shifting into Bear, and the current talent data (build 1.60.1.70959) gives rage on Bear shift and energy on Cat shift.

open_questions.why: Only Method lists it.

open_questions.text: What is Holy Strike's baseline cooldown on the live build?

open_questions.text: Does Verigan's Fist have a Forever-specific Holy proc?
open_questions.why: The knowledge base says so from a booster site; no fetched guide confirms it.

open_questions.why: It was moved from Retribution to Holy, not deleted; Method still recommends it.

open_questions.why: That loop makes both untakeable under the arrow rule; it looks like a datamining artefact. The path takes Intimidation at 30 (after Bestial Swiftness, as the deep dive says) and Bestial Wrath at 40, as every guide does. A strict validator will flag Intimidation.

open_questions.why: ForeverDB says unknown; Warcraft Tavern lists a Zephras Isle quest for Skyborne only.

open_questions.why: Only Method (and the booster site in the existing KB) mention it; no datamined quest data found.

open_questions.why: Its text only gives bracket totals; the order within each bracket is mine, checked for legality (Blade Flurry at 32 and Adrenaline Rush at 42 match its intro).

open_questions.why: A beta article measured wand hits well above their tooltip and suspected a bug; no live confirmation found.

open_questions.why: Only a beta report (Kami-labs, 3 Oct) was fetched; search snippets disagree on Strength vs Intellect.

open_questions.why: Method and Warcraft Tavern rank it first and last; no datamined stat conversion was found.

open_questions.why: The guide table lists both Totemic Recall and Totemic Projection; the development notes mention only the rename to Totemic Call.

open_questions.why: Warcraft Tavern lists quest names but only says rewards are staves, off-hands, robes and wands.

open_questions.why: An older KB line says Horde mages may train with Jessa Weaver in Dalaran; no page fetched this session confirmed it.

open_questions.why: An older KB line mentions it; no page fetched this session confirms it.

open_questions.why: Mobalytics returned 403; known only through Kami-labs' bracket summary.

open_questions.text: Is the Voidwalker or Succubus the better drain-tank pet after the pet health cut?
open_questions.why: Guides predate or ignore the Nov 2 change to 2 health per Stamina.

open_questions.text: Tiger's Fury on the live build.
open_questions.why: Only beta-era sources discuss it; the current Warcraft Tavern table omits it, which suggests removal.

open_questions.text: The Balance tree data has arrows both ways between Nature's Majesty and Nature's Splendor.
open_questions.why: One of them must be a data artefact (an arrow cannot point up); the checker here only enforces downward arrows. It does not affect the Feral path.

open_questions.text: Does Poised (32) change the opener?
open_questions.why: It cuts the next energy ability by 10 after leaving combat at full energy; no guide says how to use it yet.

alternatives: Icy Veins (40/11/0) adds Demonic Embrace 5, Demonic Aegis 2, Fel Vitality 2 instead of Unholy Power, Soul Harvest, Amplify Curse
Kami-Labs (40/0/11) adds Improved Shadow Bolt 5, Bane 5, Curse of Exhaustion 1 instead of Unholy Power, Malevolence, Improved Life Tap
ForeverDB (43/0/8) adds Bane 5, Cataclysm 3 instead of Unholy Power, Grim Reach, Fel Vitality
Warcraft Tavern (41/7/3) adds Improved Shadow Bolt 3, Demonic Energies 2 instead of Grim Reach, Soul Harvest, Fel Vitality
Method (41/10/0) adds Demonic Energies 2, Fel Vitality 2 instead of Soul Harvest, Amplify Curse, Wrack
